name: Ovarian Cancer
remarks: Epithelial ovarian cancer: risk stratification, high-risk surveillance,
diagnosis, primary/interval cytoreductive surgery, platinum-taxane
chemotherapy, PARP-inhibitor maintenance, surveillance, recurrence,
second-line therapy and terminal decline.
ENCOUNTER DISCIPLINE: ModSynthea gives each person a single encounter
reservation (State.java Encounter/EncounterEnd). Every Encounter opened
here reaches an EncounterEnd before any Delay or Guard, and every Delay
sits between an EncounterEnd and the next Encounter. The only Delays
inside an open encounter are Primary_Surgery_Stay, Interval_Surgery_Stay
(inpatient lengths of stay) and Hospice_Stay (hospice benefit period).
The pre-fix module opened exactly one wellness Encounter and never closed
it, so genetic testing, surgery, every chemotherapy cycle, PARP
maintenance and all recurrence care were recorded with no encounter of
this module's own open - HealthRecord.currentEncounter() attached them to
whatever stale visit happened to be last in the record, or minted a
'First Wellness' encounter. All clinical content is now inside an
explicit, closed encounter of the right class.
CALIBRATION TARGETS (per-state remarks carry the arithmetic):
- Average-risk women (98.5%): age-banded annual incidence rising from
0.7e-4 at 40-44 to 3.0e-4 at 60-84, i.e. ~1.1-1.4% lifetime, matching
SEER 2017-2021 ovarian cancer incidence (age-specific rates ~7/100,000
at 40-44 rising to ~28/100,000 at 70-74) and the SEER lifetime risk of
roughly 1 in 78-87 women.
- BRCA1/2 carriers (0.3% of women): 2%/yr from age 40, i.e. ~40-45%
cumulative by age 80 after competing mortality (Kuchenbaecker, JAMA
2017;317:2402 - ovarian cancer risk to 80 of 44% for BRCA1, 17% for
BRCA2). Risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy is NOT modelled, so this
arm is the untreated-carrier penetrance.
- Women with an affected first-degree relative but no identified mutation
(1.2%): ~3x the population rate (Stratton, Br J Obstet Gynaecol 1998
meta-analysis: RR ~3.1 for one affected first-degree relative).
- Population-weighted lifetime risk = 0.985 x ~1.14% + 0.012 x ~3.4%
- Stage at diagnosis, weighted over the histology mix, is ~19% I, 8% II,
45% III, 28% IV, matching SEER 2018-2022 (localised 17%, regional 20%,
distant 58%).
- Recurrence after first-line therapy: ~1.5%/yr for stage I-II and
~25%/yr for stage III-IV, blending to the ~20%/yr platinum-sensitive
figure, with a genuine 5-year sustained-remission discharge.
- Cause-specific mortality among diagnosed women lands near 50%, against
a SEER 2018-2022 5-year relative survival of ~51%.
ATTRIBUTES (all module-local, including histology/stage: 'histology' and
'cancer_stage' were shared with pancreatic_cancer.json and were renamed
to 'ovarian_histology' / 'ovarian_stage' by the cross-module
attribute-rename task -- verified by grep that no other module reads
the new names):
Ovarian Cancer            - ConditionOnset entry set at diagnosis; used
as the 'reason' pointer on treatment-phase
encounters, procedures and medications
Recurrent Ovarian Cancer  - ConditionOnset entry set at first recurrence
(also the stacking guard for that onset)
ovarian_cancer_risk       - average | family_history | high_brca
ovarian_histology         - high_grade_serous | endometrioid |
clear_cell | mucinous | low_grade_serous
ovarian_stage             - FIGO stage I..IV, as a plain string
ecog_status               - ECOG performance status 0..3, as an integer
last_ca125                - most recent CA-125 in U/mL. Observation
states cannot assign_to_attribute (the field
is declared on AttributeAssignableState and
Procedure only, so Gson silently drops it on
an Observation), so each value is drawn by a
SetAttribute and read back by the
Observation through its 'attribute' field
ovarian_chemo_cycles      - completed first-line chemotherapy cycles
ovarian_second_line_cycles- completed second-line chemotherapy cycles
ovarian_surveillance_visits - completed post-treatment surveillance visits
ovarian_recurrences       - number of recurrences experienced
ovarian_parp_status       - active | completed | stopped
Congenital risk stratum, assigned once at birth. Only the stratum is
assigned here - disease onset is rerolled every year (or every six
months in the carrier arm) in the loops below.
BRCA1/2 pathogenic-variant carriers are ~0.2-0.4% of unselected women
(Maxwell, Genet Med 2016; gnomAD founder-adjusted estimates); 0.3% is
used. A further ~1.2% of women have an affected first-degree relative
without an identified mutation.
NCCN Genetic/Familial High-Risk Assessment recommends BRCA testing
from age 25 for known-family-mutation carriers; testing and the
gynaecologic surveillance that follows are offered here from 30.
Outside every loop, so it fires exactly once - no stacking guard
needed.
Six-monthly CA-125 plus transvaginal ultrasound is the surveillance
regimen offered to carriers who decline or defer risk-reducing
salpingo-oophorectomy (NCCN; SGO). It does not reduce mortality, which
is why it is confined to the 0.3% carrier arm and is not offered to
average-risk women - USPSTF 2018 (JAMA 319:588) recommends AGAINST
screening average-risk women for ovarian cancer.

remarks: 2%/yr from age 40. This loop runs on a ~6-month pass, so
Cumulative to age 80 = 1 - 0.98^40 = 55% before competing mortality,
~40-45% realised - Kuchenbaecker (JAMA 2017;317:2402) reports ovarian
cancer risk to 80 of 44% (BRCA1) and 17% (BRCA2) in unselected
carriers who have not had risk-reducing surgery.

remarks: Annual pass. Three times the average-risk rate for the same age band
(Stratton, Br J Obstet Gynaecol 1998: RR ~3.1 with one affected
first-degree relative): 4.5e-4/yr from 45-59 and 9.0e-4/yr from 60.
Average-risk women get NO surveillance encounters - USPSTF 2018 (JAMA
319:588) recommends against screening asymptomatic average-risk women
for ovarian cancer, and PLCO/UKCTOCS found no mortality benefit. This
loop is a pure annual incidence reroll and generates no health-record
activity until disease onset.
Age-banded annual incidence, approximating SEER 2017-2021 age-specific
ovarian cancer incidence (about 7/100,000 at 40-44, 11 at 45-49, 15 at
Bands are evaluated oldest-first because ComplexTransition takes the
first condition that is true.
Cumulative for a woman who survives to 90:
= 1.14%, and ~1.38% for one who survives to 100. SEER puts the
lifetime risk of an ovarian cancer diagnosis at roughly 1.1-1.3%.
BRCA-associated ovarian cancer is overwhelmingly high-grade serous
(Mavaddat, J Natl Cancer Inst 2012).
Interval between biological onset and clinical presentation. Ovarian
cancer symptoms (bloating, early satiety, pelvic pain) are non-
specific; Goff (JAMA 2004) found a median 3-4 month symptom duration
before diagnosis.

at presentation and is typically in the hundreds for advanced serous
disease.

remarks: One diagnosis code for every histology - the histology itself lives in
the 'ovarian_histology' attribute. The pre-fix module split the diagnosis
across 93796005 and 93934004 (both of which the export map sends to
ICD-10 C56.9), which fragmented every downstream count.
Outside every loop: a person can only be diagnosed once.
High-grade serous carcinoma presents at an advanced stage in about
90% of cases (Prat, Int J Gynaecol Obstet 2014; SEER stage
distribution). Replaces the pre-fix Set_Cancer_Stage, whose
'value_set' dict was silently deserialised into a LinkedTreeMap, so
every later 'cancer_stage == I' comparison threw
'Cannot compare LinkedTreeMap to String' at runtime.
Endometrioid, clear cell, mucinous and low-grade serous carcinomas are
far more often confined to the pelvis at diagnosis. Weighted with the
serous router over the histology mix this yields ~19% I, 8% II, 45%
III, 28% IV overall, against SEER 2018-2022 (localised 17%, regional
20%, distant 58%).
Baseline ECOG performance status in first-line ovarian cancer trials
(GOG-218, ICON7) is 0 in roughly half and 2 or worse in under 20%.
Replaces the pre-fix Set_ECOG_Status, whose 'range' dict was another
silently-dropped non-scalar SetAttribute value.
Early-stage disease goes straight to primary cytoreductive surgery.
For stage III-IV, neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by interval
debulking is now the majority pathway in the US (Vergote, NEJM 2010;
Wright, J Clin Oncol 2016 ASCO/SGO guideline).
Genuine inpatient length of stay after cytoreductive surgery; one of
the three Delays in this module allowed to sit inside an open
encounter.
Stage IA/IB grade 1 disease is observed after surgery; everything
else gets adjuvant platinum-taxane chemotherapy (NCCN Ovarian Cancer
guideline).
One closed outpatient encounter per 21-day chemotherapy cycle, so
each infusion lands on its own claim with its own date of service.
Clinician-administered infusion: administration:true routes this to a
professional/outpatient claim line through rxnorm_hcpcs_map (J9045)
rather than to a Part D dispensing event, and administration rows
cannot stack, so no MedicationEnd is needed.
Three cycles before interval debulking, three after, per EORTC 55971
(Vergote, NEJM 2010).
Three neoadjuvant cycles are already done; the shared adjuvant loop
below runs to a total of six.
Six cycles of carboplatin/paclitaxel is the standard first-line course
PARP-inhibitor maintenance after a response to first-line platinum:
SOLO-1 (Moore, NEJM 2018) established olaparib for BRCA-mutated
advanced disease, PRIMA/PAOLA-1 extended maintenance to a wider
advanced-stage population. Early-stage disease is not a maintenance
indication, so stage I-II uptake is nominal.
Olaparib is an ORAL PARP inhibitor the patient takes at home, so it is
a dispensed prescription (Part D), not administration:true. The code
is the RxNorm SCD 'olaparib 150 MG Oral Tablet' (1942487) rather than
the ingredient concept 1597582, because only a clinical-drug concept
can be resolved to an NDC for the PDE export.
Fixed 2-year course (SOLO-1), ended by Stop_Olaparib_Course after 8
quarterly surveillance visits, or early at recurrence.
Quarterly clinical review with CA-125 for the first years after
first-line therapy (NCCN Ovarian Cancer surveillance schedule).

remarks: Stage-specific annual recurrence hazard converted to this loop's
quarterly pass with p_pass = 1 - (1 - p_annual)^0.25:
stage I-II   6%/yr  -> 0.0153 per pass
stage III-IV 25%/yr -> 0.0685 per pass
Weighted over the stage mix (~27% early, ~73% advanced) that is the
~20%/yr platinum-sensitive relapse rate. Over the 5 years before
sustained-remission discharge it gives ~26% cumulative relapse for
early-stage and ~76% for advanced disease, against the ~70-80% of
advanced-stage patients who relapse within 3 years (Ledermann, Ann
Oncol 2013 ESMO guideline).
The pre-fix module rolled 25% per 4.5-month pass with no exit, so
every diagnosed woman relapsed and then died in the same instant.
Twenty quarterly visits is five relapse-free years - the genuine
remission exit the pre-fix module lacked. The person leaves the module
alive; competing mortality is the lifecycle module's job.
Stacking guard: Recurrent_Disease sits inside a loop that a person can
re-enter, so the ConditionOnset only fires on the first pass, when its
assign_to_attribute target is still nil.
A second relapse after second-line chemotherapy goes to best
supportive care rather than a third cytotoxic line; this also bounds
the treatment loop.
About 60% of first relapses occur more than six months after platinum
and are retreated with a platinum doublet; the rest are
platinum-resistant and get single-agent pegylated liposomal
doxorubicin (CALYPSO, Pujade-Lauraine J Clin Oncol 2010; AURELIA).
CALYPSO reported ~65% objective response to carboplatin-PLD in
platinum-sensitive relapse; half of the arm re-enters a surveillance
remission here rather than progressing.
Single-agent PLD in platinum-resistant relapse achieves a response in
only ~12-20% (AURELIA chemotherapy arm), so most of this arm
progresses.
Interval from documented progression to the palliative-care handoff.
A bounded hospice benefit period, the third and last Delay allowed to
sit inside an open encounter here. Well under the linter's 90-day
warning threshold.
Roughly two hospice benefit periods on average (~3-4 months from
hospice enrolment to death). Death is recorded here with the encounter
already closed, and is separated from the recurrence event by the
second-line course, the progression interval and hospice - typically
6-20 months, never the same instant.
